title: The Disk Substructures at High Angular Resolution Program (DSHARP). VIII. The Rich Ringed Substructures in the AS 209 Disk
question: What is the ring/gap substructure of the AS 209 disk in 1.25 mm dust continuum and 12CO 2-1 emission at 5 au resolution, and what could cause it?

data.angular_resolution: continuum beam 38 mas x 36 mas; CO beam 95 mas x 70 mas
data.sensitivity: continuum rms 19 uJy/beam; CO rms 0.8 mJy/beam per channel

what.value: Midplane temperature profile used to estimate snowline locations

evidence.quote: using the midplane temperature derived by (cite: Andrews2009)

what.value: Hydrodynamical simulation of AS 209 (planet at 99 au, 0.087 MJ)

evidence.quote: The planet responsible for the gaps has a mass of 0.087 M$_J$.

recipe.method: CASA clean with multiscale, taper (continuum), Keplerian mask (CO)

recipe.goal: Fit radial profile of rings in uv-plane
recipe.method: Sum of concentric Gaussian rings, Hankel transform to visibilities, fit to deprojected radially averaged binned visibilities
key_parameters: uv-points 10 to 10000 kλ in 10 kλ steps; 27 free parameters (23 ring, 4 geometry)
assumptions: Axisymmetric emission; number of rings chosen by visual inspection

recipe.goal: CO moment map and radial profile
recipe.method: Moment-zero integrated -3 to 14 km/s, clip S/N<3, azimuthally averaged deprojected profile of East side

evidence.quote: presents 4 main gaps or emission decrements in the outer disk, near 45, 75, 120 and 210 au.

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channels and continuum subtraction for CO
Flux calibrator and flux scale uncertainty
Weighting/relative weights when combining the three projects' data
score_reason: Public data and a clear parametric model, but imaging and MCMC details are deferred to another paper or missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a well-defined ring model with numeric table of best-fit parameters.
